item.title: 1971: Just Weeks After Winning His Second World Series Championship
item.description: Just weeks after winning his second World Series championship, Pittsburgh Pirates manager Danny Murtaugh announces his retirement. The 53-year-old Murtaugh has a history of health issues and was briefly hospitalized during 1971 for chest pain; his decision ends the third of four terms he will serve as the team's manager. The Pirates name coach and former centerfielder Bill Virdon as Murtaugh's successor. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 2024: Gallegos Signed a Minor League Contract
item.description: On November 23, 2024, Gallegos signed a minor league contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers that included an invitation to major league spring training. Photo: Johnmaxmena2 (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2024: Rico Carty, 85, Left Fielder From 1963–1979
item.description: Rico Carty, 85, left fielder from 1963–1979 and the batting champion for the National League in 1970, his solo All-Star season. Carty was also a member of the Ivan Allen Jr. Braves Museum and Hall of Fame. Photo: Atlanta Braves (Public domain).

item.title: 2021: McKay Underwent Surgery for Thoracic Outlet Syndrome (TOS)
item.description: On November 23, 2021, McKay underwent surgery for thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS).

item.title: 2021: Bill Virdon, 90, Outfielder for the St. Louis Cardinals
item.description: Bill Virdon, 90, outfielder for the St. Louis Cardinals and Pittsburgh Pirates from 1955 to 1968 and manager for the Pirates, New York Yankees, Houston Astros and Montreal Expos from 1972 to 1984. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 2015: The Los Angeles Dodgers Hired Dave Roberts
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers hired Dave Roberts as their new manager. Roberts will succeed Don Mattingly, who mutually parted ways with the Dodgers last month after five years with the team. Roberts, whose father is an African-American former Marine and mother is a Japanese-American, becomes the first minority manager of the storied franchise that signed the first African-American player, Jackie Robinson. Photo: U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Elias Carrero) (Public domain).

item.title: 2015: Georgia State Submitted an Alternative Proposal for Redeveloping
item.description: On November 23, 2015, Georgia State submitted an alternative proposal for redeveloping Turner Field, where portions of the current ballpark would be rebuilt into a mixed retail and housing development and a new football-specific stadium would be constructed north of Turner Field along with the new baseball field. Photo: Zpb52 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2013: Laird Signed a Minor League Deal
item.description: Laird signed a minor league deal with the Kansas City Royals on November 23, 2013. Photo: TSUBAME98 (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2013: After the Announcement of the NWL's Return to Kenosha
item.description: After the announcement of the NWL's return to Kenosha, fans submitted suggestions for the team's name, and the winning suggestion of 'Kingfish' was revealed at the team's launch party on November 23, 2013.

item.title: 2012: Hal Trosky Jr., 76, Who Pitched Briefly for the Chicago White Sox
item.description: Hal Trosky Jr., 76, who pitched briefly for the Chicago White Sox during the 1958 season; son and namesake of the slugging first baseman of the 1930s. Photo: Apex Photography (Public domain).

item.title: 2009: Joe Mauer of the Minnesota Twins Becomes Only the Second Catcher
item.description: Joe Mauer of the Minnesota Twins becomes only the second catcher in 33 years to win the American League Most Valuable Player Award, finishing first in a near-unanimous vote. Mauer, who set a major league record for highest batting average by a catcher and won his third batting title, receives 27 of 28 first-place votes and 387 points in balloting by the BBWAA. New York Yankees teammates Mark Teixeira (225 points)… Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2009: Hale Was Named the New Red Sox Bench Coach
item.description: On November 23, 2009, Hale was named the new Red Sox bench coach. Photo: Keith Allison from Owings Mills, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2007: Al Yates, 62, Backup Outfielder for the 1971 Milwaukee Brewers
item.description: Al Yates, 62, backup outfielder for the 1971 Milwaukee Brewers.

item.title: 2001: Bo Belinsky, 64, Pitcher Who Enjoyed a 10-Win Rookie Season in 1962
item.description: Bo Belinsky, 64, pitcher who enjoyed a 10-win rookie season in 1962 with the Los Angeles Angels, including the first no-hitter on the West Coast, but whose raucous personal life derailed his promising career. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1990: Baudilio "Bo" Díaz, 37, Venezuelan Catcher Who Appeared in 993 Games
item.description: Baudilio "Bo" Díaz, 37, Venezuelan catcher who appeared in 993 games between 1977 and 1989 for the Boston Red Sox, Cleveland Indians, Philadelphia Phillies and Cincinnati Reds; batted .333 for Phils in the 1983 World Series and selected All-Star in both major leagues (1979, 1987).

item.title: 1990: Former Boston Red Sox, Philadelphia Phillies
item.description: Former Boston Red Sox, Philadelphia Phillies and Cincinnati Reds catcher Baudilio (Bo) Díaz is crushed to death when a rooftop satellite dish topples over at his home in Venezuela. He was 37. Photo: Metate yearbook of Pomona College (Public domain).

item.title: 1988: The New York Yankees Sign Steve Sax
item.description: The New York Yankees sign Steve Sax, granted free agency from the Los Angeles Dodgers on November 4, to a three-year, $4 million contract. Three-time NL All-Star Sax, 28, has been the Dodgers' everyday second baseman since 1982. Photo: Nathan Rupert from San Diego, California, USA (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1977: The Boston Red Sox Sign Right-Handed Starting Pitcher Mike Torrez
item.description: The Boston Red Sox sign right-handed starting pitcher Mike Torrez, a free agent formerly with the arch-rival New York Yankees, to a seven-year, $2.5 million contract. In addition to his two complete-game victories in the 1977 World Series, Torrez had won 14 games (losing 12) for the Bombers in 1977. Photo: Boston Red Sox (Public domain).

item.title: 1966: Chicago White Sox Outfielder Tommie Agee Is Voted American League
item.description: Chicago White Sox outfielder Tommie Agee is voted American League Rookie of the Year, gathering 16 of the 18 votes. Kansas City Athletics pitcher Jim Nash gets the other two votes. Agee had been brought up briefly the past four seasons before finding a permanent spot in 1966. Photo: Bernard Gotfryd (Public domain).

item.title: 1964: After 20 Seasons and 356 Victories, Most-Ever by an MLB Left-Hander
item.description: After 20 seasons and 356 victories, most-ever by an MLB left-hander, Warren Spahn and the Braves sever their relationship when Milwaukee sells the future Hall of Famer's contract to the New York Mets. Spahn, 43, had posted his poorest season in 1964—going 6–13 (5.29) in 38 games. Determined to prolong his playing career, he had turned down the Braves' offer of three off-field jobs in their organization. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1962: Los Angeles Dodgers Shortstop Maury Wills
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Maury Wills, whose 104 stolen bases broke a major league season-record set by Ty Cobb, wins the National League Most Valuable Player Award. In a controversial vote, Wills beats out teammate Tommy Davis, who led the league with a .346 batting average and 153 RBI. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1960: Los Angeles Dodgers Outfielder Frank Howard Is Selected NL Rookie
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Frank Howard is selected NL Rookie of the Year with 12 of 24 votes. The six-foot, seven-inch (2.01 m) Howard belted 23 home runs during the regular season. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1951: The New York Yankees Send Young Catcher Clint Courtney to the St
item.description: The New York Yankees send young catcher Clint Courtney to the St. Louis Browns in exchange for pitcher Jim McDonald. Courtney, a scrapper despite being the first major-league catcher to wear eyeglasses, had appeared in one game for New York. He'll appear in 945 more American League contests through 1961. Photo: Bowman Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 1948: Hack Wilson, 48, Hall of Fame Center Fielder for Four Different Clubs
item.description: Hack Wilson, 48, Hall of Fame center fielder for four different clubs during 12 seasons from !923–1934, most prominently with the Chicago Cubs between 1926 and 1931, who finished his career with a lifetime .307 batting average, 244 home runs, 1,063 RBI and four home run titles, hitting 56 long balls in 1930, to set a National League record that stood for 68 years, while driving in 191 runs in the same season, which… Photo: Conlon, Charles Martin, 1868-1945 (Photographer) (Public domain).

item.title: 1943: Culminating a Three-Month-Long Investigation
item.description: Culminating a three-month-long investigation, Commissioner Kenesaw Mountain Landis rules that Philadelphia Phillies owner William D. Cox is permanently ineligible to hold office or be employed in "Organized Baseball" for having bet on his own team. Photo: Arturo Pardavila III from Hoboken, NJ, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1930: At the Polo Grounds, St. Louis Browns Outfielder Red Badgro
item.description: At the Polo Grounds, St. Louis Browns outfielder Red Badgro, playing for the NFL New York Giants, catches a touchdown pass against the Green Bay Packers. It is the third TD catch of the season for Badgro, all from quarterback Benny Friedman. In 1981, Badgro will be elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Photo: David Shapinsky from Washington, D.C., United States (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1888: The World Champion New York Giants Announce the Sale of Star Player
item.description: The World Champion New York Giants announce the sale of star player and leader of the Brotherhood of Professional Baseball Players, John Montgomery Ward, to the Washington Nationals for $12,000. The deal will fall through after Ward refuses to abide by the sale. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).
